text:
maria: Quick pulse — hosted saw three short bursts yesterday that ate into reserved GPU capacity, exposing a ~7% commit gap. Can we decompose where the delta came from? :eyes:
jonah: Do you have the time windows? guessing embeddings/long-context generations.
maria: Peak windows: 02:50–03:30 UTC, 11:10–11:20 UTC, 21:05–21:20 UTC. Total delta ~420 reserved-GPU-minutes vs forecast.
priya: pulling logs now, but initial scrub shows a lot of small embedding batches from a handful of API keys + a spike of long-chat jobs.
priya: snippet from our quick query:
```
pool, product_tag, gpu_minutes
hosted-eu, embeddings, 210
hosted-us, chat-long, 135
hosted-us, retries/replays, 75
```
priya: notable: `retries/replays` bucket is higher than usual — looks like a client-side retry storm (3 keys).
kai: autoscaler attempted to spin additional hosted instances but the reserved-only policy pinned several jobs to committed pools, so burst pool didn't absorb everything.
infra-bot: autoscaler: failed to allocate extra burst nodes at 02:55 UTC due to quota constraints (API rate limit). Incident link: https://infra.internal/INC-4421 :warning:
jonah: so two contributors: higher request count (embeddings batching patterns) + routing policy that kept traffic on reserved nodes.
maria: @finance-bot can you estimate incremental cost from using reserved vs burst for that 420 GPU-minutes? rough ballpark is fine.
finance-bot: Rough calc: 420 GPU-minutes * (hosted on-demand rate $0.08/min - reserved amortized $0.03/min) = $21.00 incremental. Also potential overage penalties if we exceeded provider commits.
jonah: action items: 1) short-term routing change to allow compatible jobs to overflow to burst pool for next 24h, 2) throttle low-priority embedding keys (heuristic), 3) open infra ticket to relax pinned policy and investigate autoscaler quota failure.
priya: I'll open the ticket and attach a query that finds top offending API keys and request patterns. Will post PR for routing tweak (small change in route table TTL + tag matching).
kai: I'll check provider quota fallout and request temporary quota bump for the burst pool if needed.
maria: also pinging CS to check if those three keys belong to a single customer doing a replay/ingest; we should notify them. @jonah can you craft a one-liner for CS?
jonah: sure — "We observed repeated retries from your integration that consumed reserved capacity; we recommend batching client-side calls or switching to our burst plan for heavy embedding workloads."
maria: thanks. Let's reconvene after the routing change and the ticket. Short-term goal: eliminate >50% of the unexpected reserved consumption overnight. :thumbsup:
